─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n376\t\n377\t/// Retry wrapper for subprocess spawns that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n378\t///\n379\t/// ETXTBSY (\"Text file busy\") occurs when the kernel blocks execution of a binary\n380\t/// that has a write-mode file descriptor still open. This is a genuine race condition:\n381\t///\n382\t/// 1. A process writes a binary to disk and closes the file descriptor.\n383\t/// 2. The kernel's page cache and filesystem synchronization haven't fully completed.\n384\t/// 3. Another process immediately attempts to `exec()` the same binary.\n385\t/// 4. The kernel returns ETXTBSY (errno 26) because the file is still marked for write.\n386\t///\n387\t/// This is most common with:\n388\t/// - Freshly-extracted upgrade binaries executed immediately\n389\t/// - Test fixtures written and chmod'd immediately before use\n390\t/// - Any binary that's written to disk and executed in quick succession\n391\t///\n392\t/// The race is narrow (typically <100ms) but real. Retrying with a short backoff\n393\t/// is the correct fix — the file descriptor is already closed, we're just waiting\n394\t/// for the kernel to finish its internal bookkeeping.\n395\t///\n396\t/// # Parameters\n397\t///\n398\t/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n399\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n400\t/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n401\t///\n402\t/// # Returns\n403\t///\n404\t/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n405\t/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n406\t///\n407\t/// # When to use this helper\n408\t///\n409\t/// Use this wrapper whenever spawning a subprocess that may have been written to\n410\t/// disk immediately before execution:\n411\t///\n412\t/// - Freshly-installed or updated binaries\n413\t/// - Test fixtures created during test setup\n414\t/// - Any executable extracted from an archive and immediately run\n415\t///\n416\t/// Do NOT use this for long-running processes or stable system binaries — the\n417\t/// retry overhead is unnecessary and ETXTBSY is unlikely in those cases.\n418\t///\n419\t/// # Example\n420\t///\n421\t/// ```no_run\n422\t/// use std::path::Path;\n423\t/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry;\n424\t///\n425\t/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n426\t/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/binary\");\n427\t/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n428\t///     || async {\n429\t///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n430\t///             .arg(\"--version\")\n431\t///             .output()\n432\t///             .await\n433\t///     },\n434\t///     5,\n435\t///     20,\n436\t/// ).await?;\n437\t/// # Ok(())\n438\t/// # }\n439\t/// ```\n440\tpub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry<F, Fut, T>(\n441\t    spawn_fn: F,\n442\t    max_attempts: u32,\n443\t    backoff_ms: u64,\n444\t) -> std::io::Result<T>\n445\twhere\n446\t    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n447\t    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n448\t{\n449\t    let mut last_err = None;\n450\t    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n451\t        match spawn_fn().await {\n452\t            Ok(output) => {\n453\t                if attempt > 0 {\n454\t                    debug!(\n455\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n456\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n457\t                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n458\t                        \"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n459\t                        attempt + 1\n460\t                    );\n461\t                }\n462\t                return Ok(output);\n463\t            }\n464\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n465\t                last_err = Some(e);\n466\t                warn!(\n467\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n468\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n469\t                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n470\t                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n471\t                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\",\n472\t                    attempt + 1,\n473\t                    max_attempts,\n474\t                    backoff_ms\n475\t                );\n476\t                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms)).await;\n477\t            }\n478\t            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n479\t        }\n480\t    }\n481\t    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting MAX_ATTEMPTS\"))\n482\t}\n483\t\n484\t/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` calls that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n485\t///\n486\t/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry` for subprocess spawns that\n487\t/// return a `Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned\n488\t/// process (e.g., for timeout handling with `kill_on_drop`).\n489\t///\n490\t/// # Parameters\n491\t///\n492\t/// * `spawn_fn` - An async This variant uses **exponential backoff** with jitter, making it more suitable for\n515\t/// high-concurrency scenarios where multiple processes might race for the same binary.\n516\t/// Exponential backoff prevents thundering herd problems that linear backoff can cause.\n517\t///\n518\t/// The backoff formula is: `base_ms * 2^attempt + random_jitter`, where:\n519\t/// - `base_ms` is the initial delay (default: 20ms)\n520\t/// - `attempt` is the current retry number (0-indexed)\n521\t/// - `random_jitter` is ±25% of the calculated delay to prevent synchronization\n522\t///\n523\t/// Example backoff sequence with base_ms=20:\n524\t/// - Attempt 1: ~20ms (15-25ms with jitter)\n525\t/// - Attempt 2: ~40ms (30-50ms with jitter)\n526\t/// - Attempt 3: ~80ms (60-100ms with jitter)\n527\t/// - Attempt 4: ~160ms (120-200ms with jitter)\n528\t/// - Attempt 5: ~320ms (240-400ms with jitter)\n529\t///\n530\t/// # Parameters\n531\t///\n532\t/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n533\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n534\t/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n535\t///\n536\t/// # Returns\n537\t///\n538\t/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n539\t/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n540\t///\n541\t/// # When to use exponential vs linear backoff\n542\t///\n543\t/// Use exponential backoff when:\n544\t/// - Spawning multiple processes concurrently that might race for the same binary\n545\t/// - Running in high-concurrency environments (CI, parallel tests)\n546\t/// - Dealing with slow filesystems where the race window might be longer\n547\t///\n548\t/// Use linear backoff (`spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry`) when:\n549\t/// - Spawning a single process in isolation\n550\t/// - The race window is known to be very short (<50ms)\n551\t/// - Minimal latency is more important than thundering herd prevention\n552\t///\n553\t/// # Example\n554\t///\n555\t/// ```no_run\n556\t/// use std::path::Path;\n557\t/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential;\n558\t///\n559\t/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n560\t/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/freshly-written-binary\");\n561\t/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential(\n562\t///     || async {\n563\t///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n564\t///             .arg(\"--version\")\n565\t///             .output()\n566\t///             .await\n567\t///     },\n568\t///     10,\n569\t///     20,\n570\t/// ).await?;\n571\t/// # Ok(())\n572\t/// # }\n573\t/// ```\n574\tpub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential<F, Fut, T>(\n575\t    spawn_fn: F,\n576\t    max_attempts: u32,\n577\t    base_ms: u64,\n578\t) -> std::io::Result<T>\n579\twhere\n580\t    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n581\t    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n582\t{\n583\t    use rand::Rng;\n584\t\n585\t    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n586\t    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n587\t\n588\t    let mut last_err = None;\n589\t    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n590\t\n591\t    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n592\t        match spawn_fn().await {\n593\t            Ok(output) => {\n594\t                if attempt > 0 {\n595\t                    debug!(\n596\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n597\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n598\t                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n599\t                        \"ETXTBSY exponential retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n600\t                        attempt + 1\n601\t                    );\n602\t                }\n603\t                return Ok(output);\n604\t            }\n605\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n606\t                last_err = Some(e);\n607\t\n608\t                // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n609\t                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n610\t\n611\t                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n612\t                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n613\t                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n614\t                let delay = exponential_delay\n615\t                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n616\t                    .saturating_sub(jitter_range);\n617\t\n618\t                warn!(\n619\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n620\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n621\t                    delay_ms = delay,\n622\t                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n623\t                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n624\t                    attempt + 1,\n625\t                    max_attempts,\n626\t                    delay\n627\t                );\n628\t                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay)).await;\n629\t            }\n630\t            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n631\t        }\n632\t    }\n633\t\n634\t    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n635\t}\n636\t\n637\t/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n638\t///\n639\t/// Specialized version of Use this for synchronous `std::process::Command` spawns\n757\t/// in non-async contexts.\n758\t///\n759\t/// # Parameters\n760\t///\n761\t/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n762\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n763\t/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n764\t///\n765\t/// # Returns\n766\t///\n767\t/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n768\t/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n769\tpub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential<F, T>(\n770\t    spawn_fn: F,\n771\t    max_attempts: u32,\n772\t    base_ms: u64,\n773\t) -> std::io::Result<T>\n774\twhere\n775\t    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<T>,\n776\t{\n777\t    use rand::Rng;\n778\t\n779\t    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n780\t    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n781\t\n782\t    let mut last_err = None;\n783\t    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n784\t\n785\t    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n786\t        match spawn_fn() {\n787\t            Ok(output) => {\n788\t                if attempt > 0 {\n789\t                    debug!(\n790\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n791\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n792\t                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential\",\n793\t                        \"ETXTBSY sync exponential retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n794\t                        attempt + 1\n795\t                    );\n796\t                }\n797\t                return Ok(output);\n798\t            }\n799\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n800\t                last_err = Some(e);\n801\t\n802\t                // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n803\t                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n804\t\n805\t                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n806\t                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n807\t                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n808\t                let delay = exponential_delay\n809\t                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n810\t                    .saturating_sub(jitter_range);\n811\t\n812\t                warn!(\n813\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n814\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n815\t                    delay_ms = delay,\n816\t                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential\",\n817\t                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n818\t                    attempt + 1,\n819\t                    max_attempts,\n820\t                    delay\n821\t                );\n822\t                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay));\n823\t            }\n824\t            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n825\t        }\n826\t    }\n827\t\n828\t    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n829\t}\n830\t\n831\t/// Synchronous retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n832\t///\n833\t/// ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// ETXTBSY (\"Text file busy\") occurs when the kernel blocks execution of a binary\n/// that has a write-mode file descriptor still open. This is a genuine race condition:\n///\n/// 1. A process writes a binary to disk and closes the file descriptor.\n/// 2. The kernel's page cache and filesystem synchronization haven't fully completed.\n/// 3. Another process immediately attempts to `exec()` the same binary.\n/// 4. The kernel returns ETXTBSY (errno 26) because the file is still marked for write.\n///\n/// This is most common with:\n/// - Freshly-extracted upgrade binaries executed immediately\n/// - Test fixtures written and chmod'd immediately before use\n/// - Any binary that's written to disk and executed in quick succession\n///\n/// The race is narrow (typically <100ms) but real. Retrying with a short backoff\n/// is the correct fix — the file descriptor is already closed, we're just waiting\n/// for the kernel to finish its internal bookkeeping.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n///\n/// # When to use this helper\n///\n/// Use this wrapper whenever spawning a subprocess that may have been written to\n/// disk immediately before execution:\n///\n/// - Freshly-installed or updated binaries\n/// - Test fixtures created during test setup\n/// - Any executable extracted from an archive and immediately run\n///\n/// Do NOT use this for long-running processes or stable system binaries — the\n/// retry overhead is unnecessary and ETXTBSY is unlikely in those cases.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use std::path::Path;\n/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry;\n///\n/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/binary\");\n/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n///     || async {\n///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n///             .arg(\"--version\")\n///             .output()\n///             .await\n///     },\n///     5,\n///     20,\n/// ).await?;\n/// # Ok(())\n/// # }\n/// ```\npub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry<F, Fut, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    backoff_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n{\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn().await {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n                return Ok(output);\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n                warn!(\n                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms\n                );\n                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms)).await;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting MAX_ATTEMPTS\"))\n}\n\n/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` calls that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry` for subprocess spawns that\n/// return a `Child` process. std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>>,\n{\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(spawn_fn, max_attempts, backoff_ms).await\n}\n\n/// Retry wrapper for subprocess spawns with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// This variant uses **exponential backoff** with jitter, making it more suitable for\n/// high-concurrency scenarios where multiple processes might race for the same binary.\n/// Exponential backoff prevents thundering herd problems that linear backoff can cause.\n///\n/// The backoff formula is: `base_ms * 2^attempt + random_jitter`, where:\n/// - `base_ms` is the initial delay (default: 20ms)\n/// - `attempt` is the current retry number (0-indexed)\n/// - `random_jitter` is ±25% of the calculated delay to prevent synchronization\n///\n/// Example backoff sequence with base_ms=20:\n/// - Attempt 1: ~20ms (15-25ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 2: ~40ms (30-50ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 3: ~80ms (60-100ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 4: ~160ms (120-200ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 5: ~320ms (240-400ms with jitter)\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n///\n/// # When to use exponential vs linear backoff\n///\n/// Use exponential backoff when:\n/// - Spawning multiple processes concurrently that might race for the same binary\n/// - Running in high-concurrency environments (CI, parallel tests)\n/// - Dealing with slow filesystems where the race window might be longer\n///\n/// Use linear backoff (`spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry`) when:\n/// - Spawning a single process in isolation\n/// - The race window is known to be very short (<50ms)\n/// - Minimal latency is more important than thundering herd tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n///             .arg(\"--version\")\n///             .output()\n///             .await\n///     },\n///     10,\n///     20,\n/// ).await?;\n/// # Ok(())\n/// # }\n/// ```\npub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential<F, Fut, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    base_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n{\n    use rand::Rng;\n\n    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn().await {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY exponential retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n                return Ok(output);\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n\n                // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n\n                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n                let delay = exponential_delay\n                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n                    .saturating_sub(jitter_range);\n\n                warn!(\n                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    delay_ms = delay,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    delay\n                );\n                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay)).await;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n}\n\n/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential` for subprocess spawns that\n/// return a `Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned process\n/// (e.g., for timeout handling with `kill_on_drop`).\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(Child)` - The spawned child process on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential_child<F, Fut>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    base_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>>,\n{\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential(spawn_fn, max_attempts, base_ms).await\n}\n\n// ─── Synchronous ETXTBSY retry helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Synchronous retry wrapper for subprocess spawns that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// This is the sync equivalent of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry`, using `std::thread::sleep`\n/// instead of `tokio::time::sleep`. Use this for synchronous `std::process::Command` spawns\n/// in non-async contexts.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync<F, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    backoff_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<T>,\n{\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY sync retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n                return Ok(output);\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n                warn!(\n                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms\n                );\n                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms));\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting MAX_ATTEMPTS\"))\n}\n\n/// Synchronous retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` calls that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync` for subprocess spawns that\n/// return a `std::process::Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned\n/// process (e.g., for timeout handling) in synchronous contexts.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(Child)` - The spawned child process on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_child<F>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    backoff_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<std::process::Child>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<std::process::Child>,\n{\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync(spawn_fn, max_attempts, backoff_ms)\n}\n\n/// Synchronous retry wrapper for subprocess spawns with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// This is the sync equivalent of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential`, using `std::thread::sleep`\n/// instead of `tokio::time::sleep`. Use this for synchronous `std::process::Command` spawns\n/// in non-async contexts.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential<F, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    base_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<T>,\n{\n    use rand::Rng;\n\n    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY sync exponential retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n                return Ok(output);\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n\n                // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n\n                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n                let delay = exponential_delay\n                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n                    .saturating_sub(jitter_range);\n\n                warn!(\n                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    delay_ms = delay,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    delay\n                );\n                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay));\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n}\n\n/// Synchronous retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential` for subprocess spawns that\n/// return a `std::process::Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned\n/// process (e.g., for timeout handling) in synchronous contexts.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(Child)` - The spawned child process on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child<F>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    base_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<std::process::Child>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<std::process::Child>,\n{\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential(spawn_fn, max_attempts, base_ms)\n}\n\n/// Result of a version check.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum VersionCheck {\n    /// Version is OK or unknown (no known issues).\n    Ok,\n    /// Known-bad version detected with specific issues.\n    KnownBad {\n        version: String,\n        issues: Vec<String>,\n    },\n    /// Version check failed (bf not found, parse error, etc.).\n    Failed { reason: String },\n}\n\n/// Spawn `<br_path> --version>`, retrying briefly on ETXTBSY.\n///\n/// Wraps `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry` to handle the specific case of checking\n/// bead-forge version. The retry logic handles the race condition where a\n/// binary written to disk moments earlier (e.g., during upgrade or test setup)\n/// transiently reports \"Text file busy\" (errno 26).\nasync fn spawn_version_check(br_path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<std::process::Output> {\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n        || async {\n            tokio::process::Command::new(br_path)\n                .arg(\"--version\")\n                .output()\n                .await\n        },\n        5,\n        20,\n    )\n    .await\n}\n\n/// Check the bead-forge version and detect known-bad versions.\n///\n/// This function runs `bf --version` and parses the output to detect\n/// versions with known bugs. The primary use case is detecting bead-forge\n/// 0.2.0, which has a bug where `--limit 0` returns an empty set instead\n/// of all beads.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// - `VersionCheck::Ok` if the version is not known to be bad\n/// - `VersionCheck::KnownBad` if a known-bad version is detected\n/// - `VersionCheck::Failed` if the version check failed\npub async fn check_bead_forge_version(br_path: &Path) -> VersionCheck {\n    let timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);\n\n    let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout, spawn_version_check(br_path)).await {\n        Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n        Ok(Err(e)) => {\n            return VersionCheck::Failed {\n                reason: format!(\"failed to spawn bf --version: {e}\"),\n            };\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            return VersionCheck::Failed {\n                reason: \"bf --version timed out after 5s\".to_string(),\n            };\n        }\n    };\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return VersionCheck::Failed {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"bf --version exited with code {}\",\n                output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1)\n            ),\n        };\n    }\n\n    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n    let version = stdout.trim().to_string();\n\n    if version.is_empty() {\n        return VersionCheck::Failed {\n            reason: \"bf --version produced no output\".to_string(),\n        };\n    }\n\n    // Extract version number by taking the second word if present\n    // This handles formats like \"bf 0.2.0\" or \"br 0.2.0-github\"\n    let version_number = version.split_whitespace().nth(1).unwrap_or(&version);\n\n    // Check against known-bad version prefixes\n    let mut issues = Vec::new();\n    for &(bad_prefix, issue) in KNOWN_BAD_VERSIONS {\n        if version_number.starts_with(bad_prefix) {\n            issues.push(issue.to_string());\n        }\n    }\n\n    if !issues.is_empty() {\n        VersionCheck::KnownBad { version, issues }\n    } else {\n        VersionCheck::Ok\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run version handshake and emit telemetry for known-bad versions.\n///\n/// This is called during worker boot to detect and warn about known-bad\n/// bead-forge versions. It emits a WARN-level telemetry event if issues\n/// are found.\npub async fn run_version_handshake(br_path: &Path) {\n    match check_bead_forge_version(br_path).await {\n        VersionCheck::Ok => {\n            tracing::debug!(\"bead-forge version check passed\");\n        }\n        VersionCheck::KnownBad { version, issues } => {\n            for issue in &issues {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    version = %version,\n                    issue = %issue,\n                    \"bead-forge version has known bugs — explicit limits will be used to work around\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        VersionCheck::Failed { reason } => {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                reason = %reason,\n                \"failed to check bead-forge version — cannot detect known-bad versions\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Corruption detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Known error strings that 6\", // SQLITE_LOCKED = table is locked\n];\n\n/// Known error strings that indicate br sync conflicts.\npub const SYNC_CONFLICT_MARKERS: &[&str] = &[\"SYNC_CONFLICT\", \"JSONL is newer\", \"sync .any(|marker| msg.contains(marker))\n}\n\n/// Check if an error message indicates SQLite database is locked (transient condition).\n///\n/// Returns `true` if the message contains any known lock body: &'a str,\n    pub labels: &'a [&'a str],\n}\n\n// ─── BeadStore trait ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Abstract interface to the bead bool {\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// Whether an error indicates a transient lock according to this store's backend.\n    fn is_lock_error(&self, _message: &str) -> bool {\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// Whether an error indicates a sync conflict according to this store's backend.\n    fn is_sync_conflict(&self, _message: &str) -> bool {\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// List all beads with no incomplete blockers (ready to work on).\n    ///\n    /// Returns an empty `Vec` when the queue is empty — that is not an error.\n    /// Returns `Err` if JSON parsing or br invocation fails.\n    async fn ready(&self, filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>>;\n\n    /// List ALL beads in the workspace (no readiness/filter checks).\n    ///\n    /// Used by Knot strand for three-state verification — a DIFFERENT code\n    /// path from `ready()` to avoid v1's false-positive bug.\n    async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>>;\n\n    /// Fetch a single bead by ID.\n    async fn show(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead>;\n\n    /// Fetch a bead together with the number of claim-related history entries\n    /// the backend exposed for it.\n    ///\n    /// Most backends do not include event history in their normal bead\n    /// projection, so the default implementation reports no count.  A\n    /// backend that does expose history can override this to let NEEDLE stop\n    /// retrying a bead before another claim mutation grows its JSON record.\n    async fn show_with_claim_history(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<(Bead, Option<u32>)> {\n        Ok((self.show(id).await?, None))\n    }\n\n    /// Fetch operator/agent notes when the backend exposes them.\n    ///\n    /// Backends without a notes projection return `None`; this keeps notes a\n    /// capability rather than forcing it into NEEDLE's common bead model.\n    async fn notes(&self, _id: &BeadId) -> Result<Option<String>> {\n        Ok(None)\n    }\n\n    /// Attempt to atomically claim a bead (set status=in_progress, assignee=actor).\n    ///\n    /// Returns a `ClaimResult` describing the outcome:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)` — success, returns the full bead.\n    /// - `RaceLost { claimed_by }` — another worker got there first.\n    /// - `NotClaimable { reason }` — bead not in a claimable state.\n    async fn claim(&self, id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>;\n\n    /// Atomically find and claim the next available bead (server-selected).\n    ///\n    /// This is the preferred method for multi-worker scenarios as it eliminates\n    /// race conditions: the server selects the bead and assigns it in a single\n    /// BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. Two workers calling this simultaneously will\n    /// always receive distinct beads.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a `ClaimResult` describing the outcome:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)` — success, returns the full bead.\n    /// - `NotClaimable { reason }` — no beads available to claim.\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>;\n\n    /// Release a claimed bead back to open (e.g., after agent failure).\n    async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Quarantine a bead by setting status=blocked (e.g., after it exceeds the\n    /// consecutive-failure threshold in `OutcomeConfig::quarantine_after_failures`).\n    ///\n    /// Unlike `release`, this deliberately does NOT clear the assignee or return\n    /// the bead to a claimable state — the whole point is to stop Pluck from\n    /// re-selecting it until a human (or a future auto-split) intervenes.\n    async fn block(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Clear the assignee on a bead without changing its status.\n    ///\n    /// Used by mend to heal open beads with stale assignees (e.g., after reopen).\n    async fn clear_assignee(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush local bead changes to JSONL before release.\n    ///\n    /// Runs `br sync --flush-only` to ensure any local writes are persisted\n    /// to JSONL before attempting to release a bead. N child creations plus\n    /// N dependency links must commit together: otherwise a crash between the\n    /// `create` and the `dep add` (SIGKILL, OOM, pod eviction) leaves an orphaned\n    /// child with no dependency link, and the parent never unblocks — plan.md\n    /// Phase 5.3, Race 3.\n    ///\n    /// The parent is deliberately **not** closed: NEEDLE keeps a split parent\n    /// open/blocked while its children are worked.\n    ///\n    /// The default implementation performs the historical non-atomic sequence\n    /// (`create_bead` + `add_dependency`, one child at a time). Mock stores rely\n    /// on it, and bf-backed stores fall back to it when the atomic path is\n    /// unavailable. Backends that can run a transactional batch (bf) override\n    /// this to make the whole split crash-safe.\n    async fn split_bead(\n        &self,\n        parent_id: &BeadId,\n        children: &[NewChild<'_>],\n    ) -> Result<Vec<BeadId>> {\n        let mut created = Vec::with_capacity(children.len());\n        for child in children {\n            let child_id = self\n                .create_bead(child.title, child.body, child.labels)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create child bead: {}\", child.title))?;\n            self.add_dependency(&child_id, parent_id)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| {\n                    format!(\"failed to add dependency: {child_id} blocks {parent_id}\")\n                })?;\n            created.push(child_id);\n        }\n        Ok(created)\n    }\n\n    /// Remove a dependency link: `blocker_id` blocks `blocked_id`.\n    ///\n    /// Uses `br dep remove <blocked_id> <blocker_id>`.\n    async fn remove_dependency(&self, blocked_id: &BeadId, blocker_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Run `br doctor --repair` and return the report.\n    async fn doctor_repair(&self) -> Result<RepairReport>;\n\n    /// Run `br doctor` (without `--repair`) to check database health.\n    ///\n    /// Returns warnings if any issues are detected, without attempting to fix them.\n    async fn doctor_check(&self) -> Result<RepairReport>;\n\n    /// Full database rebuild from the configured backend's durable checkpoint.\n    ///\n    /// The existing SQLite file set remains in a rollback backup until the\n    /// public backend import and doctor verification both succeed.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Err` if rebuild or verification fails; the original database\n    /// is restored in that case.\n    async fn full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Check if this store has a valid bead store (i.e., has a `.beads/` directory).\n    ///\n    /// Returns `true` if the workspace contains a `.beads/` directory, `false` otherwise.\n    /// This is used by strands to distinguish between \"no home store configured\" (expected,\n    /// benign for roam-only workers) and \"home store is broken\" (unexpected, problem).\n    fn has_valid_store(&self) -> bool;\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests etxtbsy_retry_linear_timing() {\n        let call_count = Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(0));\n        let call_count_clone = Arc::clone(&call_count);\n\n        let start = Instant::now();\n\n        let result = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n            || {\n                let count = Arc::clone(&call_count_clone);\n                async move {\n                    let attempt = count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    if attempt < 2 {\n                        Err::<_, io::Error>(make_etxtbsy_error())\n                    } else {\n                        Ok::<_, io::Error>(b\"success\".to_vec())\n                    }\n                }\n            },\n            5,\n            50,\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        let elapsed = start.elapsed();\n\n        assert!(result.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(call_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 3); // 2 failures + 1 success\n\n        // With 2 retries at 50ms each, should take ~100ms\n default_version_command() -> Vec<String> {\n    vec![\"--version\".to_string()]\n}\n\nimpl BeadBackend {\n    /// Run a binary with --version flag and parse its output to extract the backend name.\n    ///\n    /// This function spawns a binary with the provided version command (e.g., `[\"--version\"]`),\n    /// captures its stdout, and parses the output to identify which bead backend it is.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `binary_path` - Path to the binary to execute\n    /// * `version_command` - Arguments to pass for version info (e.g., `[\"--version\"]`)\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// The backend name extracted from the version output (e.g., \"bead\", \"bf\").\n    ///\n    /// # Errors\n    /// * If the binary cannot be found or spawned\n    /// * If the binary exits with a non-zero status\n    /// * If the output cannot be parsed\n    pub fn parse_backend_name_from_version(\n        binary_path: &Path,\n        version_command: &[String],\n    ) -> Result<String> {\n        // Spawn the binary with version command\n        let output = Command::new(binary_path)\n            .args(version_command)\n            .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n            .output()\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to spawn binary '{}' for version check\",\n                    binary_path.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        // Check exit code\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n            bail!(\n                \"binary '{}' exited with status {}: {}\",\n                binary_path.display(),\n                output.status,\n                stderr.trim()\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Parse stdout to extract backend name\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n        let stdout = stdout.trim();\n\n        // Try to match common version output patterns\n        // Expected formats:\n        // - \"bead 0.x.y\" or \"bead 0.x.y (details)\"\n        // - \"bf 0.x.y\" or \"bf 0.x.y (details)\"\n        // - \"beads-rust 0.x.y\"\n\n        // Pattern 1: First word before whitespace (e.g., \"bead\" from \"bead 0.1.3\")\n        let first_word_pattern = Regex::new(r\"^(\\S+)\\s\").unwrap();\n        if let Some(caps) = first_word_pattern.captures(stdout) {\n            if let Some(name) = caps.get(1) {\n                return Ok(name.as_str().to_string());\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Pattern 2: If no space, entire output is the name (e.g., just \"bead\")\n        if !stdout.is_empty() && !stdout.contains(char::is_whitespace) {\n            return Ok(stdout.to_string());\n        }\n\n        bail!(\n            \"unable to parse backend name from version output: '{}'\",\n            stdout\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Classify an error using only this backend's declared markers.\n    pub fn error_contains_any(&self, message: &str, markers: &[String]) -> bool {\n        let message = message.to_lowercase();\n        markers\n            .iter()\n            .any(|marker| message.contains(&marker.to_lowercase()))\n    }\n\n    /// Validate everything that could otherwise fail during the first claim.\n    pub fn validate(&self, source: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.name.trim().is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"descriptor {} has an empty backend name\", source.display());\n        }\n        if self.binary.trim().is_empty() {\n            bail!(\n                \"descriptor {} for backend '{}' has an empty binary\",\n                source.display(),\n                self.name\n            );\n        }\n        if self.identity_pattern.trim().is_empty() {\n            bail!(\n                \"descriptor {} for backend '{}' is missing identity_pattern\",\n                source.display(),\n                self.name\n            );\n        }\n        Regex::new(&self.identity_pattern).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"descriptor {} for backend '{}' has invalid identity_pattern {:?}\",\n                source.display(),\n                self.name,\n                self.identity_pattern\n            )\n        })?;\n        if self.version_command.is_empty() {\n            bail!(\n                \"descriptor {} for backend '{}' has an empty version_command\",\n                source.display(),\n                self.name\n            );\n        }\n\n        for required in REQUIRED_OPERATIONS {\n            if !self.operations.contains_key(*required) {\n                bail!(\n                    \"descriptor {} for backend '{}' is missing required operation '{}'\",\n                    source.display(),\n                    self.name,\n                    required\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        for (operation, spec) in &self.operations {\n            if spec.timeout_secs == Some(0) {\n                bail!(\n                    \"descriptor {} operation '{}' has a zero timeout\",\n                    source.display(),\n                    operation\n                );\n            }\n            if let Some(strategy) = &spec.strategy {\n                validate_strategy_name(source, operation, strategy)?;\n            }\n            validate_placeholders(source, operation, &spec.argv)?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nfn validate_placeholders(source: &Path, operation: &str, argv: &[String]) -> Result<()> {\n    let placeholder = Regex::new(r\"\\{([^{}]+)\\}\").expect(\"static placeholder regex is valid\");\n    let allowed = allowed_placeholders(operation);\n\n    for argument in argv {\n        let mut remainder = argument.clone();\n        for capture in placeholder.captures_iter(argument) {\n            let full = capture.get(0).expect(\"capture zero exists\").as_str();\n            let name = capture.get(1).expect(\"capture one exists\").as_str();\n            if !allowed.contains(&name) {\n                bail!(\n                    \"descriptor {} operation '{}' has unresolvable placeholder '{{{}}}'\",\n                    source.display(),\n                    operation,\n                    name\n                );\n            }\n            remainder = remainder.replacen(full, \"\", 1);\n        }\n        if remainder.contains('{') || remainder.contains('}') {\n            bail!(\n                \"descriptor {} operation '{}' has malformed placeholder in {:?}\",\n                source.display(),\n                operation,\n                argument\n            );\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn allowed_placeholders(operation: descriptors, overriding built-ins by name.\npub fn load_bead_backends(\n    dir: &Path,\n    built_ins: &[BeadBackend],\n) -> Result<HashMap<String, BeadBackend>> {\n    let mut backends = &self.backend.verified_against;\n                // Extract version number (e.g., \"bf 0.4.1\" -> \"0.4.1\")\n                let version_part = verified.split_whitespace().nth(1).unwrap_or(verified);\n                // Simple check: if requirement says \"<= 0.2.0\" and we're at \"0.4.1\", it doesn't match\n                if let Some(req_version) = requirement.strip_prefix(\"<=\") {\n                    let req_version = req_version.trim();\n                    // Very basic version comparison - should use semver crate in production\n                    // For now: \"0.4.1\" > \"0.2.0\" means quirk doesn't apply (return false)\n                    // If current version > required version, quirk does NOT match\n                    version_part <= req_version\n                } else {\n                    // Unknown requirement format - conservatively apply the quirk\n                    true\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub async fn run_operation(\n        &self,\n        name: &str,\n        values: &HashMap<&str, String>,\n    ) -> Result<String> {\n        let args = Result<Self::Value, A::Error>\n        where\n            A: SeqAccess<'de>,\n        {\n            let mut count = 0u32;\n            while let Some(event) = sequence.next_element::<EventTypeOnly>()? {\n                if matches!(\n                    event.event_type.as_deref(),\n                    Some(\"claimed\") | Some(\"assignee_changed\") | Some(\"claim\")\n                ) {\n                    count = count.saturating_add(1);\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(Some(count))\n        }\n\n        fn visit_none<E>(self) -> Result<Self::Value, E>\n        where\n            E: de::Error,\n        {\n            Ok(Some(0))\n        }\n\n        fn visit_unit<E>(self) -> Result<Self::Value, E>\n        where\n            E: de::Error,\n        {\n            Ok(Some(0))\n        }\n    }\n\n    deserializer.deserialize_any(ClaimEventVisitor)\n}\n\nfn parse_beads_with_claim_history(\n    shape: ParseShape,\n    output: &str,\n) -> Result<Vec<(Bead, Option<u32>)>> {\n    if output.trim().is_empty() {\n        return Ok(Vec::new());\n    }\n\n    let records = match shape {\n        ParseShape::JsonArray =>  vec![record]\n            } else {\n                serde_json::from_str::<Vec<BeadWithClaimHistory>>(output)?\n            }\n        }\n        ParseShape::JsonLines => {\n            // Same dual full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        if !matches!(self.backend.name.as_str(), \"bead-rs\" | \"bead-forge\") {\n            bail!(\n                \"descriptor-driven full rebuild is not self.workspace.join(\".beads/issues.jsonl\")\n        } else {\n            self.workspace.join(\".beads/checkpoint\")\n        };\n        if !checkpoint.exists() {\n            bail!(\n SQLite file set recoverable until import and\n        // doctor verification both succeed. A failed import must never turn a\n        // repairable store into an empty or partially initialized one.\n        let db_paths = [\n            self.workspace.join(\".beads/beads.db\"),\n {\n                path.with_extension(format!(\n                    \"{}needle-rebuild-backup\",\n                    path.extension()\n                        .and_then(|extension| extension.to_str())\n                        .map(|extension| format!(\"{extension}.\"))\n                        .unwrap_or_default()\n                ))\n            })\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n        for backup in &backup_paths {\n            if backup.exists() {\n                bail!(\n                    \"refusing to overwrite prior rebuild backup {}\",\n                    backup.display()\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        for (path, backup) in db_paths.iter().zip(&backup_paths) {\n            if path.exists() {\n                if let Err(preserve_error) = tokio::fs::rename(path, backup).await {\n                    for (original, preserved) in db_paths.iter().zip(&backup_paths) {\n                        if preserved.exists() {\n                            let _ = tokio::fs::rename(preserved, original).await;\n                        }\n                    }\n                    return Err(preserve_error).with_context(|| {\n                        format!(\n                            \"failed to preserve {} as {}; prior files were restored\",\n                            path.display(),\n                            backup.display()\n                        )\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let rebuild = async {\n            if self.backend.name == \"bead-forge\" DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n                )\n                .await?;\n            } else {\n                self.run_argv(\n                    \"full_rebuild.init\",\n                    &[\"init\".to_string()],\n                    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n                )\n                .await?;\n                let checkpoint = checkpoint\n                    .to_str()\n \"import-only\".to_string(),\n                    \"--input\".to_string(),\n                    checkpoint.to_string(),\n                    \"--restore-into-empty\".to_string(),\n                    \"--actor\".to_string(),\n                    \"needle\".to_string(),\n                ];\n                self.run_argv(\"full_rebuild.import\", &args, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS)\n                    .await?;\n            }\n            let report = self.doctor_check().await?;\n            if !report.warnings.is_empty() {\n                bail!(\n                    \"database still has issues after rebuild: {:?}\",\n                    report.warnings\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        .await;\n\n        if let Err(rebuild_error) = rebuild {\n            let mut rollback_errors = Vec::new();\n            for path in &db_paths {\n                if path.exists() {\n                    if let Err(error) = tokio::fs::remove_file(path).await {\n                        rollback_errors.push(format!(\n                            \"failed to remove incomplete rebuild {}: {error}\",\n                            path.display()\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            for (path, backup) in db_paths.iter().zip(&backup_paths) {\n                if backup.exists() {\n                    if let Err(error) = tokio::fs::rename(backup, path).await {\n                        rollback_errors.push(format!(\n                            \"failed to restore {} from {}: {error}\",\n                            path.display(),\n                            backup.display()\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            if !rollback_errors.is_empty() {\n                bail!(\n                    \"rebuild failed ({rebuild_error:#}); rollback was incomplete: {}\",\n                    rollback_errors.join(\"; \")\n                );\n            }\n            return Err(rebuild_error.context(\"rebuild failed; original database restored\"));\n        }\n\n        for backup in &backup_paths {\n            if backup.exists() {\n                tokio::fs::remove_file(backup).await.with_context(|| {\n                    format!(\n                        \"rebuild succeeded but failed to remove {}\",\n                        backup.display()\n &BeadId,\n        children: &[NewChild<'_>],\n    ) -> Result<Vec<BeadId>> {\n        if matches!(\n            self.strategy(\"split\")?,\n            ParsedStrategy::Split(super::SplitStrategy::TransactionalBatch)\n        ) {\n            if children.is_empty() {\n                return Ok(Vec::new());\n            }\n            let mut operations = Vec::with_capacity(children.len() * 2);\n            for child in children {\n                operations.push(serde_json::json!({\n                    \"op\": \"create\",\n                    \"title\": child.title,\n                    \"description\": child.body,\n                    \"labels\": child.labels,\n                }));\n            }\n            for index in 0..children.len() {\n                operations.push(serde_json::json!({\n                    \"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\",\n                    \"id\": parent_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"blocker\": format!(\"@{index}\"),\n                }));\n            }\n            let payload = serde_json::to_string(&operations)?;\n            let args = vec![\"batch\".to_string(), \"--json\".to_string(), payload];\n            let stdout = self.run_argv(\"split\", &args, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS).await?;\n            let ids = parse_batch_created_ids(&stdout);\n            if ids.len() != children.len() {\n                bail!(\n                    \"backend '{}' committed split for {} children but returned {} IDs\",\n                    self.backend.name,\n                    children.len(),\n                    ids.len()\n                );\n            }\n            return Ok(ids);\n        }\n\n        let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(children.len());\n        for child in children {\n            let id = self\n                .create_bead(child.title, child.body, child.labels)\n                .await?;\n            self.add_dependency(&id, parent_id).await?;\n            ids.push(id);\n        }\n        Ok(ids)\n    }\n\n    async fn remove_dependency(&self, blocked_id: &BeadId, blocker_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        self.mutate(\n async fn doctor_repair(&self) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n        let stdout = self.run_operation(\"doctor_repair\", &HashMap::new()).await?;\n        Ok(parse_doctor_output(&stdout))\n    }\n    async fn doctor_check(&self) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n        let stdout = self.run_operation(\"doctor_check\", &HashMap::new()).await?;\n        Ok(parse_doctor_output(&stdout))\n    }\n    async fn full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        if !matches!(self.backend.name.as_str(), \"bead-rs\" | \"bead-forge\") {\n            bail!(\n                \"descriptor-driven full rebuild is not enabled for backend '{}'\",\n                self.backend.name\n            );\n        }\n\n        let checkpoint = if self.backend.name == \"bead-forge\" {\n            self.workspace.join(\".beads/issues.jsonl\")\n        } else {\n            self.workspace.join(\".beads/checkpoint\")\n        };\n        if !checkpoint.exists() {\n            bail!(\n                \"refusing to rebuild backend '{}' without checkpoint {}\",\n                self.backend.name,\n                checkpoint.display()\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Keep the complete SQLite file set recoverable until import and\n        // doctor verification both succeed. A failed import must never turn a\n        // repairable store into an empty or partially initialized one.\n        let db_paths = [\n            self.workspace.join(\".beads/beads.db\"),\n            self.workspace.join(\".beads/beads.db-wal\"),\n            self.workspace.join(\".beads/beads.db-shm\"),\n        ];\n        let backup_paths = db_paths\n            .iter()\n            .map(|path| {\n                path.with_extension(format!(\n                    \"{}needle-rebuild-backup\",\n                    path.extension()\n                        .and_then(|extension| extension.to_str())\n                        .map(|extension| format!(\"{extension}.\"))\n                        .unwrap_or_default()\n                ))\n            })\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n        for backup in &backup_paths {\n            if backup.exists() {\n                bail!(\n                    \"refusing to overwrite prior rebuild backup {}\",\n                    backup.display()\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        for (path, backup) in db_paths.iter().zip(&backup_paths) {\n            if path.exists() {\n                if let Err(preserve_error) = tokio::fs::rename(path, backup).await {\n                    for (original, preserved) in db_paths.iter().zip(&backup_paths) {\n                        if preserved.exists() {\n                            let _ = tokio::fs::rename(preserved, original).await;\n                        }\n                    }\n                    return Err(preserve_error).with_context(|| {\n                        format!(\n                            \"failed to preserve {} as {}; prior files were restored\",\n                            path.display(),\n                            backup.display()\n                        )\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let rebuild = async {\n            if self.backend.name == \"bead-forge\" {\n                self.run_argv(\n                    \"full_rebuild.import\",\n                    &[\"sync\".to_string(), \"--import-only\".to_string()],\n                    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n                )\n                .await?;\n            } else {\n                self.run_argv(\n                    \"full_rebuild.init\",\n                    &[\"init\".to_string()],\n                    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n                )\n                .await?;\n                let checkpoint = checkpoint\n                    .to_str()\n                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"checkpoint path is not valid UTF-8\"))?;\n                let args = vec![\n                    \"sync\".to_string(),\n                    \"import-only\".to_string(),\n                    \"--input\".to_string(),\n                    checkpoint.to_string(),\n                    \"--restore-into-empty\".to_string(),\n                    \"--actor\".to_string(),\n                    \"needle\".to_string(),\n                ];\n                self.run_argv(\"full_rebuild.import\", &args, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS)\n                    .await?;\n            }\n            let report = self.doctor_check().await?;\n            if !report.warnings.is_empty() {\n                bail!(\n                    \"database still has issues after rebuild: {:?}\",\n                    report.warnings\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        .await;\n\n        if let Err(rebuild_error) = rebuild {\n            let mut rollback_errors = Vec::new();\n            for path in &db_paths {\n                if path.exists() {\n                    if let Err(error) = tokio::fs::remove_file(path).await {\n                        rollback_errors.push(format!(\n                            \"failed to remove incomplete rebuild {}: {error}\",\n                            path.display()\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            for (path, backup) in db_paths.iter().zip(&backup_paths) {\n                if backup.exists() {\n                    if let Err(error) = tokio::fs::rename(backup, path).await {\n                        rollback_errors.push(format!(\n                            \"failed to restore {} from {}: {error}\",\n                            path.display(),\n                            backup.display()\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            if !rollback_errors.is_empty() {\n                bail!(\n                    \"rebuild failed ({rebuild_error:#}); rollback was incomplete: {}\",\n                    rollback_errors.join(\"; \")\n                );\n            }\n            return Err(rebuild_error.context(\"rebuild failed; original database restored\"));\n        }\n\n        for backup in &backup_paths {\n            if backup.exists() {\n                tokio::fs::remove_file(backup).await.with_context(|| {\n                    format!(\n                        \"rebuild succeeded but failed to remove {}\",\n                        backup.display()\n                    )\n                })?;\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n    fn has_valid_store(&self) -> bool {\n        self.workspace.join(\".beads\").is_dir()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl CliBeadStore {\n    async fn claim_via_batch(&self, id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        let shown = self.show(id).await?;\n        if shown.status != BeadStatus::Open {\n            return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: format!(\"bead is {}, not open\", shown.status),\n            });\n        }\n        if let Some(claimed_by) = shown.assignee {\n            return Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost { claimed_by });\n        }\n\n        // bf 0.4.1 removed --assignee from `update`, but its transactional\n        // batch update operation still accepts status and assignee together.\n        self.run_bf_update_batch(id, Some(\"in_progress\"), Some(actor))\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf batch update {id} (claim) failed\"))?;\n\n        let claimed = self.show(id).await?;\n        if claimed.assignee.as_deref() == Some(actor) {\n            Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(claimed))\n        } else {\n            Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost {\n                claimed_by: claimed.assignee.unwrap_or_else(|| \"(unknown)\".to_string()),\n            })\n        }\n    }\n\n    async fn run_bf_update_batch(\n        &self,\n        id: &BeadId,\n        status: Option<&str>,\n        assignee: Option<&str>,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut operation = serde_json::Map::new();\n        operation.insert(\"op\".to_string(), serde_json::json!(\"update\"));\n        operation.insert(\"id\".to_string(), serde_json::json!(id.as_ref()));\n        if let Some(status) = status {\n match shape {\n        ParseShape::JsonArray => serde_json::from_str(output).context(\"invalid JSON array\"),\n        ParseShape::JsonObject => {\n            if let Ok(bead) = serde_json::from_str::<Bead>(output) {\n                return Ok(vec![bead]);\n            }\n            let beads: Vec<Bead> = serde_json::from_str(output).context(\"invalid JSON object\")?;\n            if beads.len() != 1 {\n                bail!(\"expected one JSON object, found {}\", beads.len());\n            }\n            Ok(beads)\n        }\n        ParseShape::JsonLines => {\n            // bead-rs emits a JSON array (`[]`) for an empty result set but\n            // newline-delimited objects otherwise. Accept both shapes: treating\n            // `[]` as a parse error made Explore skip the whole workspace and\n            // Pluck fail its ready query instead of reading \"no beads\".\n            let mut beads = Vec::new();\n            for line in output.lines() {\n                let line = line.trim();\n                if line.is_empty() {\n                    continue;\n                }\n beads.extend(batch);\n                    continue;\n                }\n                beads.push(serde_json::from_str(line).context(\"invalid JSON line\")?);\n            }\n            Ok(beads)\n BeadWithClaimHistory {\n    #[serde(flatten)]\n    bead: Bead,\n    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = \"count_claim_events\")]\n    events: Option<u32>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Deserialize)]\nstruct D::Error>\nwhere\n    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,\n{\n    struct ClaimEventVisitor;\n\n    impl<'de> Visitor<'de> for ClaimEventVisitor {\n        type Value = Option<u32>;\n\n        fn Result<Self::Value, A::Error>\n        where\n            A: SeqAccess<'de>,\n        {\n            let mut count = 0u32;\n            while let Some(event) = sequence.next_element::<EventTypeOnly>()? {\n                if matches!(\n                    event.event_type.as_deref(),\n                    Some(\"claimed\") | Some(\"assignee_changed\") | Some(\"claim\")\n                ) {\n                    count = count.saturating_add(1);\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(Some(count))\n        }\n\n        fn visit_none<E>(self) -> Result<Self::Value, E>\n        where\n            E: de::Error,\n        {\n            Ok(Some(0))\n        }\n\n        fn visit_unit<E>(self) -> Result<Self::Value, E>\n        where\n            E: de::Error,\n        {\n            Ok(Some(0))\n        }\n    }\n\n    deserializer.deserialize_any(ClaimEventVisitor)\n}\n\nfn parse_beads_with_claim_history(\n    shape: ParseShape,\n    output: &str,\n) -> Result<Vec<(Bead, Option<u32>)>> {\n    if output.trim().is_empty() {\n        return Ok(Vec::new());\n    }\n\n    let records = match shape {\n        ParseShape::JsonArray => serde_json::from_str::<Vec<BeadWithClaimHistory>>(output)?,\n        ParseShape::JsonObject => {\n            if let Ok(record) = serde_json::from_str::<BeadWithClaimHistory>(output) {\n #[allow(dead_code)]\n    fn has_quirk(&self, quirk_name: &str) -> bool {\n        self.backend\n            .quirks\n            .iter()\n            .any(|q| q.name == quirk_name && &crate::bead_store::backend::BeadBackendQuirk) -> bool {\n        match &quirk.version_requirement {\n            None => true, // No version requirement means it always applies\n            Some(requirement) => {\n                // Parse the version requirement and check against verified version\n                // For now, since we only have \"<= 0.2.0\" and verified_against is \"bf 0.4.1\",\n                // the quirk should NOT apply (0.4.1 > 0.2.0)\n                // This is a simplified check - a full implementation would use semver parsing\n                let verified = &self.backend.verified_against;\n                // Extract version number (e.g., \"bf 0.4.1\" -> \"0.4.1\")\n                let version_part = verified.split_whitespace().nth(1).unwrap_or(verified);\n                // Simple check: if requirement says \"<= 0.2.0\" and we're at \"0.4.1\", it doesn't match\n                if let Some(req_version) = requirement.strip_prefix(\"<=\") {\n                    let req_version = req_version.trim();\n                    // Very basic version comparison - should use semver crate in production\n                    // For now: \"0.4.1\" > \"0.2.0\" means quirk doesn't apply (return false)\n                    // If current version > required version, quirk does NOT match\n                    version_part <= req_version\n                } else {\n                    // Unknown requirement format - conservatively apply the quirk\n                    true\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub async fn run_operation(\n        &self,\n        name: &str,\n        values: &HashMap<&str, String>,\n    ) -> Result<String> {\n        let args =
